description: Productivity page — top-level tab housing three sub-views (Plans & Tasks / Coordinator / Knowledge) backed by the productivity-stack PG tables (plans, tasks, reviews, productivity_knowledge, coordinator_decisions, snapshots). The plan/task board is a three-column read-only board: a plans list with a 'Show archived' toggle (left, 25%), a tasks-for-selected-plan list grouped by phase with a collapsible Reflection panel above it (middle, 50%), and a task-detail panel showing claims, deps, latest review summary, and worker session metadata (right, 25%). The Coordinator dashboard stacks five panels — PlanRecommendations card, the medium-confidence Recommendations queue, an LLM-driven Advisories list (advise-with-text rows from the last hour), an Escalations list of destructive auto_acted=false rows (kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, escalate, escalate-with-text), and a chronological Decision log of the last 200 coordinator_decisions filterable by rule (A-E or LLM) and action. The Knowledge browser is rendered both inline (Knowledge sub-view) and as a modal globally triggered by Ctrl+Shift+K; both modes share the same FTS-only search surface with an area-filter dropdown and click-to-expand result rows. A top-bar selector switches between the three sub-views and is also driven by the `productivity-set-view` window CustomEvent (used by useAppNavigation alias routing and by the Recommendations / Reflection / PlanRecommendations cross-component triggers). The page is a window into orchestration logic: tasks transition pending → ready → assigned → running → review → (done | needs_fix | escalated), reviews flow through a confidence-gated handler (auto-merge ≥ 0.85, user-approval queue [0.7, 0.85), coordinator action below), and the Coordinator's auto-act boundary keeps destructive actions advisory-only.

groups.name: Productivity Shell
groups.description: The page renders a top bar with a 'Productivity' heading, three sub-view tabs (Plans & Tasks, Coordinator, Knowledge) with lucide-react icons (ClipboardList, Bot, BookOpen), and a right-aligned 'Knowledge' button that opens the modal browser. Below the top bar the active sub-view is rendered into a flex-1 content area. The active sub-view defaults to 'plans' and can be switched by clicking a tab or by dispatching a `productivity-set-view` CustomEvent.

assertions.description: The page shows a 'Productivity' heading at the top of the top bar.
The top bar shows a 'Plans & Tasks' sub-view tab with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.view-tab-plans.
The top bar shows a 'Coordinator' sub-view tab with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.view-tab-coordinator.
The top bar shows a 'Knowledge' sub-view tab with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.view-tab-knowledge.

The top bar shows a right-aligned 'Knowledge' button (separate from the sub-view tab) that opens the modal knowledge browser. The button has data-ui-bridge-id productivity.open-knowledge-modal and a 'Open knowledge browser (Ctrl+Shift+K)' tooltip.

On first load the Plans & Tasks sub-view is active (data-page-id='productivity-plans' on the inner board) and its tab shows the active style (bg-primary/15 text-primary, aria-pressed='true'). The other two tabs are inactive (text-muted-foreground, aria-pressed='false').

groups.name: Visual Design — Typography
groups.description: The page uses a typography hierarchy that follows the runner's design tokens: the page-title 'Productivity' uses the `text-h2` heading class, sub-view tab labels use text-sm font-medium, panel headers use text-sm font-semibold, list-row primary text uses text-sm, and metadata/timestamps use text-xs or [11px]/[10px] muted variants. Text-visibility (foreground vs background) is also covered here because every text element must be legible against its panel background.

assertions.description: The 'Productivity' top-bar heading uses the text-h2 typography class so its font-size, weight, and tracking match the runner-wide page-title token.
Sub-view tab labels render with font-weight 500 (text-sm font-medium). Lighter weights would dilute the active/inactive visual contrast.

Panel section headings ('Plans', 'Tasks', 'Task Detail', 'Recommendations queue', 'Escalations', 'Advisories', 'Decision log', 'Coordinator suggests next plan') render with font-weight 600 (font-semibold).

Primary list text (plan title, task description, decision row reasoning) uses the `text-foreground` token which resolves to a high-contrast color against the panel `bg-card/30` background. The computed text color must NOT be the same as the parent's resolved background — text would be invisible. This is the recurring 'white text on white background' regression the spec audit catches.
assertions.precondition: At least one plan row is present.

groups.name: Visual Design — Color Scheme
groups.description: The page uses the runner's neutral panel/background tokens (`bg-background`, `bg-card/30`, `bg-card/40`) for surfaces, `border-border` for separators, and a small palette of semantic accent colors keyed to status: blue (ready/running), cyan (assigned), purple (review/reflection/advisory), amber (needs_fix/escalation/advisory-only), emerald (done/auto-acted/approve), red (escalated/decline). These accents appear on borders, badge backgrounds, and badge text.

assertions.description: The page root uses the `bg-background` token so it inherits the runner-wide app background and stays consistent with adjacent tabs.

The active sub-view tab is styled with bg-primary/15 + text-primary so it visually pops vs the muted-foreground inactive tabs. An inactive tab styled like an active one (or vice versa) breaks the user's mental model of which view is current.
assertions.precondition: The Plans sub-view is active (default).

assertions.description: Every plan-status and task-status badge is rendered with a status-specific accent (pending=muted, ready=blue, assigned=cyan, running=blue, review=purple, needs_fix=amber, done=emerald, escalated=red, cancelled=muted). All nine statuses must be visually distinguishable — using the same color for two different statuses would make the board misleading.
assertions.precondition: At least one plan with tasks is selected.

assertions.description: Panel separators (column dividers, header bottom-border, row dividers) use the `border-border` token, not hardcoded colors. This keeps the page consistent with the rest of the runner UI when the user toggles light/dark mode.

groups.name: Visual Design — Spacing & Layout
groups.description: The plan/task board uses a fixed 25% / 50% / 25% three-column flex layout with explicit minWidth on the side columns (220px plans, 260px detail). The Coordinator dashboard centers its panel stack at max-w-5xl with gap-4 between panels and p-4 internal padding. Rows in lists use border-b border-border/60 dividers with px-3 py-2 padding. Every interactive button has at least p-1 to guarantee a comfortable hit target.

assertions.description: When the Plans sub-view is active, the board renders three direct-child columns inside the data-page-id='productivity-plans' container. The leftmost (plans list) and rightmost (task detail) are shrink-0 with style width 25%; the middle is flex-1 min-w-0.
The Coordinator dashboard is centered with mx-auto and capped at max-w-5xl so panels don't stretch on ultrawide displays. The five panels render as a vertical flex stack with gap-4.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: When the knowledge modal is open it renders at max-w-3xl h-[70vh] centered over a black/40 backdrop with z-50, so it visually replaces the page without losing the page boundary entirely.
assertions.precondition: The 'Knowledge' top-bar button has been clicked or Ctrl+Shift+K has been pressed.

assertions.description: The task-detail column has min-width 260px to keep the dl status grid (Phase, Sequence, Assigned, Started, Completed) readable and to prevent file-claim paths from wrapping aggressively.

groups.name: Plans & Tasks — Three-Column Structure
groups.description: The Plans & Tasks sub-view renders three columns. LEFT (25%): PlansList with header ('Plans' h2 + Show-archived checkbox + refresh button) and a scrollable plan-row list. Each plan row shows the plan title (or markdownPath basename fallback), a PlanStatus badge, an optional 2-line summary, and the markdownPath in monospace muted text. The active plan has bg-primary/10 + border-primary left rail. MIDDLE (50%): collapsible Reflection panel above + TasksList below. The TasksList groups by phaseName (UPPERCASE phase header bg-muted/20) with rows sorted by sequenceInPhase showing the sequence #, the first line of the description, and a TaskStatus badge. Each row has a chevron to expand the full description. RIGHT (25%): TaskDetailPanel showing Status (badge + 2-col dl grid: Phase, Sequence, Assigned, Started, Completed), Expected file claims (with conflict badge when other tasks claim the same path), Depends on, Latest review summary, Worker session, and Notes.

assertions.description: The PlansList column is present with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.plan-list and renders an h2 with text 'Plans' inside its header.
The TasksList column is present with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.task-list. When no plan is selected the column shows 'Select a plan on the left to see its tasks.' italic muted text.

The TaskDetailPanel column is present with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.task-detail. When no task is selected it shows 'Select a task to see its claims, dependencies, and review history.' italic muted text.

The plans-column header contains a 'Show archived' (label text 'archived') checkbox with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.show-archived-toggle. Toggling it calls listPlansFiltered with includeArchived=true; when ON the plan list also includes plans with status 'done' or 'abandoned'. Default state is unchecked.

The task-detail panel shows an 'Expected file claims' section (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.task-claims) listing detail.task.expectedFileClaims (font-mono paths) and detail.task.expectedDirs (suffixed with '/'). When other tasks claim the same path, the row shows an amber AlertCircle with the conflicting-claim count.
assertions.precondition: A task is selected.

assertions.description: The task-detail panel shows a 'Depends on' section (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.task-deps) listing detail.task.dependsOn task IDs in monospace, or 'None.' italic muted text when empty.
assertions.precondition: A task is selected.

assertions.description: When a plan is selected, the TasksList groups its tasks by phaseName under uppercase phase headers (text-[10px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-wider, bg-muted/20). Within each phase group, rows are sorted by sequenceInPhase ascending. A task appearing under the wrong phase header indicates a TaskRow.phaseName mapping bug.
assertions.precondition: A plan with at least one task is selected.

groups.name: Coordinator Dashboard — Five-Panel Stack
groups.description: The Coordinator dashboard renders five vertically-stacked panels in a fixed order: (1) PlanRecommendations 'Coordinator suggests next plan' card; (2) RecommendationsPanel — medium-confidence approved review queue; (3) AdvisoriesPanel — LLM advise-with-text rows from the last hour; (4) EscalationsPanel — open destructive recommendations the agent flagged advisory-only; (5) DecisionLogPanel — chronological feed of last 200 coordinator_decisions rows filterable by rule (A-E or LLM) and action. Each panel is wrapped in a border-border + bg-card/30 rounded-lg section with its own header (icon + title + count chip + Refresh button) and a content area that handles error / empty / populated states.

assertions.description: The PlanRecommendations card is rendered above the Recommendations queue, with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.plan-recommendations and a 'Coordinator suggests next plan' heading.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The Recommendations queue panel is present with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-recommendations and a 'Recommendations queue' heading. Empty-state copy explicitly mentions the [0.7, 0.85) confidence band.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The Advisories panel is present with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-advisories and a 'Advisories' heading. Empty-state copy explicitly mentions advise-with-text rows from the last hour.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The Escalations panel is present with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-escalations and an 'Escalations' heading. The empty-state copy explicitly names the destructive actions (kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree).
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The Decision log panel is present with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-decision-log, a 'Decision log' heading, the static text 'last 200 rows', and rule + action filter selects with refresh button.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The five panels render in this exact top-to-bottom order: PlanRecommendations → Recommendations queue → Advisories → Escalations → Decision log. Panel ordering matters: PlanRecommendations is the user's first action prompt; Recommendations comes before Escalations because it's the most-frequent decision type; Decision log is last because it's read-only audit data.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

groups.name: Knowledge Browser — Modal & Inline Modes
groups.description: The KnowledgeBrowser renders in two modes from the same component: 'modal' (overlay with backdrop + dialog role + Esc-to-close + close X button) and 'inline' (full-height panel with no backdrop or close button). Both modes share: a Search input (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-search-input, placeholder 'Search knowledge…', Enter triggers search), an area-filter dropdown (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-area-filter, populated dynamically from distinct areas in the current hit set with 'All areas' default), a Search submit button (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-search-submit, disabled when query is blank), a results list (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-results), and a footer showing the result count. Each result row is keyed by hit.row.id with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-result-row, shows area pill + session id + score + summary, and click toggles a body disclosure rendering hit.row.body in a monospace pre block.

assertions.description: The knowledge browser shows a search input with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-search-input and placeholder 'Search knowledge…'.
assertions.precondition: The Knowledge sub-view is active or the modal is open.

assertions.description: The knowledge browser shows an area-filter dropdown with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-area-filter. The dropdown's first option is 'All areas' (value=''); subsequent options are the distinct hit.row.area values from the current result set.
assertions.precondition: The Knowledge sub-view is active or the modal is open.

assertions.description: The knowledge browser shows a Search submit button with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-search-submit. The button is disabled when the search query is blank.
assertions.precondition: The Knowledge sub-view is active or the modal is open.

assertions.description: The knowledge browser results region exists (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-results). When the user has not entered a query yet, this region shows the prompt text 'Type a query and press Enter. The knowledge table is populated by /summarize-session after each task completion.'.
assertions.precondition: The Knowledge sub-view is active or the modal is open.

assertions.description: When the modal is open the wrapping container has role='dialog', aria-modal='true', and aria-label='Knowledge browser', providing screen-reader semantics. The modal content has data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-modal.
assertions.precondition: The 'Knowledge' top-bar button has been clicked or Ctrl+Shift+K has been pressed.

assertions.description: Each rendered result row has data-ui-bridge-id productivity.knowledge-result-row, shows the area as a pill (bg-primary/10 text-primary), an optional session id (truncated to 8 chars), a score formatted to 3 decimals, and the summary text. The chevron is right-pointing when collapsed and down-pointing when expanded; expanding renders hit.row.body in a monospace pre block under the row.
assertions.precondition: A search has returned at least one result.

groups.name: Domain Logic — Task State Machine & Confidence Gates
groups.description: Per productivity-stack §2 (data model) and §5 (Coordinator state machine), every task lives in exactly one of nine states: pending → ready (when all dependsOn are done) → assigned → running → review → (done | needs_fix | escalated) — with cancelled as a terminal abort. needs_fix retries cap at 3 before forced escalation. Reviews are confidence-gated: verdict=approved AND confidence ≥ 0.85 → auto-merge (no UI surface); confidence in [0.7, 0.85) → user-approval Recommendations queue; confidence < 0.7 OR verdict in {needs_fix, escalate} → coordinator action. The board is the only surface where these state transitions are user-visible — incorrect states or transitions on display indicate a bug in the underlying tasks/reviews tables or in their derivation.

assertions.description: Every task badge rendered in the TasksList must show one of the nine known TaskStatus labels (Pending, Ready, Assigned, Running, In Review, Needs Fix, Done, Escalated, Cancelled). A blank badge or a label outside this set indicates a TASK_STATUS_STYLES mapping gap or a corrupt tasks.status value.
assertions.precondition: A plan with at least one task is selected.

assertions.description: A task displayed with status 'Ready' must have all of its detail.task.dependsOn task IDs resolved to status 'Done' in the same plan's task list. If a 'Ready' task's depends-on list contains a task still in pending/running/review, the readiness derivation in tasks.rs is broken.
assertions.precondition: A task with status 'Ready' is selected.

assertions.description: A task that has cycled through 'Needs Fix' more than 3 times should be escalated, not still showing 'Needs Fix'. The Decision log should contain a corresponding 'reassign-needs-fix' rule entry per retry, and a final 'escalate' row at the cap. Plans where the same task description appears in 'Needs Fix' for many iterations indicate the retry-cap enforcement in the Coordinator is broken.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active and the decision log has data.

assertions.description: Every card in the Recommendations queue must show a confidence percentage in the range 70%–84% inclusive. A row outside this band means the queue selection rule (verdict=approved AND confidence in [0.7, 0.85)) is broken in the reviews backend, OR a high-confidence row failed to auto-merge, OR a low-confidence row was incorrectly enqueued for user approval rather than escalated.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active and at least one recommendation is queued.

assertions.description: Every Recommendations queue card must show verdict 'approved' (rendered as the amber-300 monospace label). A 'needs_fix' or 'escalate' row appearing in this queue means the reviews backend is enqueuing rows that should have gone to the Coordinator's destructive-action path instead.
assertions.precondition: At least one recommendation is queued.

groups.name: Domain Logic — Coordinator Auto-Act Boundary
groups.description: The server-enforced auto-act boundary (productivity-stack §5) guarantees that destructive or LLM-judgement actions ALWAYS persist with auto_acted=false regardless of whether the agent claimed to act: kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, cancel-task, escalate, escalate-with-text, advise-with-text, idle-no-action. These are surfaced as advisory chips in the Decision log and route to the Escalations panel (destructive subset) or the Advisories panel (advise-with-text only). Every Decision log row also displays an 'auto' (emerald) or 'advisory' (amber) chip based on autoActed — a kill-session or force-promote-to-worktree row showing 'auto' indicates the server boundary was bypassed and is a critical safety bug.

assertions.description: Every Decision log row whose action is in {kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, escalate, escalate-with-text, advise-with-text, cancel-task, idle-no-action} must display the amber 'advisory' chip (not the emerald 'auto' chip). Showing 'auto' for one of these actions means the auto-act boundary check in coordinator.rs::act was skipped.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active and the decision log contains at least one destructive-action row.

assertions.description: Every card in the Escalations panel must have an action drawn from {kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, escalate, escalate-with-text} — these are the destructive recommendations the agent flagged advisory-only. A row with action 'assign-task' or 'merge-task' in the Escalations panel indicates getEscalations is over-fetching.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active and at least one escalation is open.

assertions.description: Every Advisories panel card must have action 'advise-with-text'. The Advisories panel is filtered client-side to action='advise-with-text' AND resolved=false AND createdAt within the last hour. A card with any other action surfaces a filter regression in CoordinatorDashboard::loadAdvisories.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active and at least one advisory is unread.

assertions.description: Each Escalations card exposes 'Approve' and 'Decline' buttons. Approve calls resolveEscalation(id, 'approve') which flips coordinator_decisions.resolved=true and refreshes both the escalation list and the decision log. Decline calls resolveEscalation(id, 'decline') with the same refresh side-effect. After resolve the row no longer appears in the Escalations panel.
assertions.precondition: At least one escalation is open.

assertions.description: Each Advisories card exposes an 'Acknowledge' button that calls acknowledgeAdvisory(decisionId) which flips coordinator_decisions.resolved=true. After acknowledgement the row disappears from the Advisories panel and no longer counts in 'N unread'. Refreshing the Decision log should show the same row but it stays visible there for audit purposes.
assertions.precondition: At least one advisory is unread.

groups.name: Reflection Panel — Aggregate Correctness
groups.description: The ReflectionPanel renders a per-plan rollup composed by the get_reflection backend command. The header shows plan title · status · short version-hash (first 8 chars). The 5-tile stat row shows totalTasks, completedTasks, escalatedTasks, avgConfidence, and knowledgeCount. Aggregate invariants per plan §2 + plan §5: avgConfidence is null when no reviews exist (rendered as '—', NOT '0%'); knowledgeCount equals the number of productivity_knowledge rows linked to this plan's tasks; totalTasks equals the count of TaskRow rows for this planId; completedTasks counts tasks with status 'Done'; escalatedTasks counts tasks with status 'Escalated'. Two list sections follow: 'Top knowledge' (top-5 entries with area pill + summary, click switches to Knowledge sub-view filtered by area) and 'Review trail' (every review row with verdict badge + confidence + relative time + open-session link).

assertions.description: When a plan is selected and the Reflection toggle is open, a panel with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.reflection-panel is rendered above the TasksList in the middle column.
assertions.precondition: A plan is selected and the Reflection toggle is open.

assertions.description: The Reflection panel shows exactly five stat tiles in a grid (Total tasks, Completed, Escalated, Avg confidence, Knowledge). Fewer indicates a missing tile; more indicates a duplicated tile.
assertions.precondition: Reflection data has loaded for the selected plan.

assertions.description: When the plan has zero reviews (reflection.avgConfidence is null), the 'Avg confidence' tile displays '—', NOT '0%' or 'NaN%'. This guards the formatConfidence helper against the empty-state regression where formatting `null * 100` would render '0%' and falsely imply zero confidence.
assertions.precondition: A plan with zero review rows is selected.

assertions.description: The 'Total tasks' tile value equals the number of TaskRow items rendered in the TasksList for the same plan. The 'Completed' tile equals the number of those rows showing the 'Done' badge. The 'Escalated' tile equals the number of those rows showing the 'Escalated' badge. A divergence between the Reflection rollup and the TasksList means the get_reflection aggregate query and the get_plan_tasks query disagree about which rows belong to the plan.
assertions.precondition: A plan with at least one task is selected and Reflection is open.

assertions.description: The 'Top knowledge' section (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.reflection-top-knowledge) renders up to 5 entries from reflection.topKnowledge, each as a clickable button with an uppercase area tag and the entry summary. Empty state shows the italic muted text "No knowledge entries linked to this plan's tasks yet." Clicking an entry dispatches productivity-set-view (knowledge) and productivity-knowledge-filter with the area.
assertions.precondition: Reflection data has loaded.

assertions.description: The 'Review trail' section (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.reflection-review-trail) renders every reflection.reviewTrail row with a verdict badge (approved=emerald, needs_fix=amber, escalate=red), a confidence percentage, an 8-char task-id prefix, a localized timestamp, and an external-link icon button that dispatches productivity-open-session for the worker session. Empty state copy mentions /auto-review.
assertions.precondition: Reflection data has loaded.

groups.name: Decision Log — Filters & Row Cap
groups.description: The Decision log panel queries getCoordinatorDecisions(limit=200, {rule, action}) and renders rows sorted by createdAt descending. The rule-filter select (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-decision-log-rule-filter) offers options 'all' (value=''), A, B, C, D, E, LLM, idle. The action-filter select (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-decision-log-action-filter) offers options 'all' plus the 11 CoordinatorActionName values: assign-task, pause-session, merge-task, reassign-needs-fix, escalate, advise-with-text, escalate-with-text, kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, cancel-task, idle-no-action. Changing either filter triggers a reload and re-renders rows. Each row shows action (color-keyed by autoActed), rule, iteration, time, optional targetId, and full reasoning.

assertions.description: The rule-filter select renders exactly 8 options corresponding to RULE_FILTER_OPTIONS: '' (all), A, B, C, D, E, LLM, idle. Missing options would silently bias the filter; extra options indicate stale code.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The action-filter select renders exactly 12 options corresponding to ACTION_FILTER_OPTIONS: '' (all), assign-task, pause-session, merge-task, reassign-needs-fix, escalate, advise-with-text, escalate-with-text, kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree, cancel-task, idle-no-action.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The Decision log shows AT MOST 200 rows even when the underlying coordinator_decisions table contains more (DECISION_LOG_LIMIT=200). The 'last 200 rows' count chip in the header is a literal label, not a dynamic value. A row count > 200 indicates the limit clause was dropped from getCoordinatorDecisions.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: Every Decision log row displays a chip on the right showing 'auto' (emerald, autoActed=true) or 'advisory' (amber, autoActed=false). The action label color tracks the same: emerald-400 when auto, amber-400 when advisory.
assertions.precondition: The decision log contains at least one row.

assertions.description: Clicking the Decision log refresh button (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-decision-log-refresh) re-runs getCoordinatorDecisions with the current rule + action filters. While loading, the button is disabled and the RefreshCw icon spins.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

groups.name: Recommendations Queue — Approve / Reject / Open Task
groups.description: Each Recommendations queue card (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-recommendation-card with data-review-id) exposes three actions: Approve (emerald), Reject (red), and Open task (muted external-link button). Approve calls approveRecommendation(reviewId) which marks the underlying review as approved and flips the task to 'done'; on success both the recommendation list and the decision log are refreshed. Reject calls rejectRecommendation(reviewId) and refreshes the recommendation list only. Open task dispatches both 'productivity-set-view' (plans) AND 'productivity-select-task' so the user lands on the plan/task board with that task pre-selected. While a row's action is in flight, all three buttons are disabled. ReviewBadge in the terminal also dispatches 'productivity-select-recommendation' which highlights a card here in amber and scrolls it into view.

assertions.description: Each recommendation card shows an Approve button with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-recommendation-approve, emerald colors (border-emerald-500/40 + bg-emerald-500/10), and a CheckCircle2 icon.
assertions.precondition: At least one recommendation is queued.

assertions.description: Each recommendation card shows a Reject button with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-recommendation-reject, red colors (border-red-500/40 + bg-red-500/10), and an XCircle icon.
assertions.precondition: At least one recommendation is queued.

assertions.description: Each recommendation card shows an 'Open task' button with data-ui-bridge-id productivity.coord-recommendation-open-task. Clicking it dispatches the productivity-set-view ('plans') and productivity-select-task (with taskId) CustomEvents. The user should observe the sub-view switch back to Plans & Tasks and the corresponding task become the active selection.
assertions.precondition: At least one recommendation is queued.

assertions.description: Clicking Approve on a recommendation card calls invoke('approve_recommendation', {reviewId}) and on success refreshes both the Recommendations queue (the row disappears) and the Decision log (a new 'merge-task' or similar audit row appears). The card's three buttons are disabled while the call is in flight.
assertions.precondition: At least one recommendation is queued.

assertions.description: When the productivity-select-recommendation CustomEvent fires with a reviewId, the matching card (matched via data-review-id) gains a yellow highlight (border-amber-400 + bg-amber-500/10) and scrolls into view smoothly. This is how the terminal-tab ReviewBadge deep-links into the queue.
assertions.precondition: A productivity-select-recommendation event has been dispatched with a queued reviewId.

groups.name: Empty / Loading / Error States
groups.description: Each panel handles three lifecycle states. LOADING: a small spinner (Loader2 animate-spin) + grey muted text (e.g. 'Loading plans…', 'Loading tasks…', 'Loading detail…', 'Computing recommendations…', 'Loading reflection…'). ERROR: a soft empty state with explanatory italic muted copy — never a crashed page (try/catch wrappers in fetchPlans / loadDecisions / etc. coerce errors into empty results so an unmigrated backend renders cleanly). EMPTY: instructional muted copy that explains how to populate the surface (e.g. 'Run /decompose-plan', 'Run /summarize-session', 'Once /coordinate is running'). The PlansList specifically renders 'Plan registry unavailable. The backend command may not be registered yet.' on error.

assertions.description: When listPlansFiltered returns an empty array (no plans), the PlansList renders the italic muted text 'No plans yet. Run /decompose-plan to populate this list.' This is the bootstrap-instruction empty state on a fresh database.
assertions.precondition: No plans exist in the database.

assertions.description: When the Recommendations queue is empty, the panel renders muted text mentioning '/auto-review' and the '[0.7, 0.85)' confidence band so users know how rows land here.
assertions.precondition: No recommendations are queued.

assertions.description: When no escalations are open, the Escalations panel renders muted text naming the destructive actions: 'kill-session, force-promote-to-worktree'. This documents the auto-act boundary directly in the UI.
assertions.precondition: No escalations are open.

assertions.description: Before the user runs a knowledge search, the results region shows the prompt 'Type a query and press Enter. The knowledge table is populated by /summarize-session after each task completion.' which directs the user to the populating command.
assertions.precondition: The Knowledge sub-view is active and no search has been run.

assertions.description: When listPlansFiltered throws (e.g. v29 migration not yet applied), the page does NOT crash — it shows 'Plan registry unavailable. The backend command may not be registered yet.' inside the plans column. The page remains navigable and the other sub-views still function.
assertions.precondition: The list_plans_filtered Tauri command throws or is missing.

groups.name: User Interactions — Toggles, Sub-View Switches, Hotkey
groups.description: Page-level interactions: clicking a sub-view tab calls setView and updates the active tab style + which sub-view component renders. The 'Knowledge' top-bar button opens the modal (not the sub-view); the modal can also be opened anywhere via Ctrl+Shift+K (useKnowledgeBrowserHotkey). The Show-archived checkbox triggers fetchPlans with includeArchived=true and re-paints the plans list. The Reflection collapse button persists its open/closed state in localStorage under productivity.reflection-open.{planId} so the choice survives plan re-selection. Clicking a plan-recommendation card's 'Open plan' switches the sub-view to plans AND selects the plan via two CustomEvents (productivity-set-view + productivity-select-plan). Esc closes the knowledge modal; clicking the backdrop or the X also closes it.

assertions.description: Clicking productivity.view-tab-coordinator switches the rendered sub-view: data-page-id changes from 'productivity-plans' to 'productivity-coordinator' and the Coordinator panels (productivity.plan-recommendations, productivity.coord-recommendations, etc.) become visible. The Plans tab loses bg-primary/15 styling; the Coordinator tab gains it.

Clicking the Show-archived checkbox (productivity.show-archived-toggle) toggles its checked state and re-runs listPlansFiltered with the new value. Plans previously hidden because their status was 'done' or 'abandoned' appear when ON; they disappear when OFF. The default state on first load is unchecked.

Pressing Ctrl+Shift+K anywhere in the runner toggles the global Knowledge modal (productivity.knowledge-modal). The hotkey is mounted via useKnowledgeBrowserHotkey at the App level and works regardless of which page is currently focused.

When the Knowledge modal is open, pressing Escape calls onClose and unmounts the modal (the backdrop and dialog disappear). Clicking the backdrop or the X (productivity.knowledge-close) has the same effect.
assertions.precondition: The Knowledge modal is open.

assertions.description: Clicking the Reflection chevron button toggles reflectionOpen and writes '1' or '0' to localStorage under productivity.reflection-open.{planId}. Re-selecting the same plan later restores the persisted state. Selecting a different plan reads its own key (default closed when no record exists).
assertions.precondition: A plan is selected.

assertions.description: Dispatching window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('productivity-set-view', { detail: { view: 'coordinator' } })) switches the sub-view without clicking a tab. ProductivityPage's effect listens for this event (reading detail.view). useAppNavigation uses this when an alias like 'productivity-coordinator' is requested via UI Bridge / pageNavigate.

groups.name: Plan Recommendations Card — Top-K Candidates
groups.description: The PlanRecommendations card at the top of the Coordinator dashboard renders up to 3 candidate plans (server-ranked by getPlanRecommendations — cheap-rule only, no LLM). Each card row shows a ListChecks icon + plan title (or planId fallback), reasoning text (e.g. '3 ready tasks, 2 idle sessions, no upcoming-claim conflicts'), and an 'Open plan' button (ArrowRight icon) that dispatches productivity-set-view (plans) and productivity-select-plan (planId) so the plan/task board lands on the candidate. The empty state explicitly directs the user to /decompose-plan on a vetted plan. The card header shows 'top {N}' where N is rows.length.

assertions.description: The PlanRecommendations card renders at the top of the Coordinator panel stack (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.plan-recommendations) with header 'Coordinator suggests next plan' and refresh button.
assertions.precondition: The Coordinator sub-view is active.

assertions.description: The card renders at most 3 plan-recommendation rows (data-ui-bridge-id productivity.plan-recommendation-card per row, with data-plan-id). A higher count means the backend's top-K cap was widened or removed.
assertions.precondition: At least one plan candidate exists.

assertions.description: When getPlanRecommendations returns no candidates, the card shows the muted text 'No plan candidates with ready/unassigned tasks. Run /decompose-plan on a vetted plan to populate this card.' This empty state explicitly mentions /decompose-plan as the populating command.
assertions.precondition: No plan candidates exist.

assertions.description: Clicking 'Open plan' dispatches the productivity-set-view ('plans') and productivity-select-plan (planId) CustomEvents. The user should observe the sub-view switch back to Plans & Tasks AND the chosen plan become selected (left-rail accent) with its tasks in the middle column.
assertions.precondition: At least one plan candidate exists.

states.name: Plans & Tasks View
states.description: The Plans & Tasks sub-view is active. The three-column board is visible: a plans list (with a 'Show archived' toggle) on the left, a collapsible Reflection panel above the phase-grouped task list in the middle, and a task-detail panel on the right. This is the default sub-view on page load.

states.name: Coordinator View
states.description: The Coordinator sub-view is active. Renders five stacked panels: a 'Coordinator suggests next plan' card (PlanRecommendations), a medium-confidence Recommendations queue with Approve/Reject/Open-task per row, an Advisories list (advise-with-text rows from the last hour with Acknowledge), an Escalations list (open destructive auto_acted=false rows with Approve/Decline), and a chronological Decision log (last 200 coordinator_decisions filterable by rule and action).

states.name: Knowledge View
states.description: The Knowledge sub-view is active. Renders the inline KnowledgeBrowser with an FTS search input, an area-filter dropdown populated dynamically from distinct hit areas, a submit button, and a results list with click-to-expand body disclosure.

states.name: Knowledge Modal
states.description: The Knowledge browser is open as a centred modal over the page (role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-label='Knowledge browser'). The originating sub-view (Plans or Coordinator) stays visible behind a black/40 backdrop. Esc, the close X, or backdrop click dismisses the modal.
